rationale.conceptual: The paper applies an established but non-trivial method combining a Conv1d-FC neural network with celestial mechanics numerical integration. Implementing the Runge-Kutta integrator and correctly sampling the resonant angles according to the ∝A_σ² distribution demands careful attention to domain details, but no novel algorithm or deep theoretical derivation is required.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of two main stages (data generation via integration, model training) plus a final evaluation step. All steps rely on standard Python libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy) with straightforward I/O; there is no complex multi-tool orchestration or fragile handoffs beyond sequential dependencies.

difficulty.reasoning: The method requires non-trivial implementation of PCR3BP numerical integration and a specific ANN architecture, but both are well-described; the pipeline is three sequential steps (data generation, training, evaluation) using standard libraries.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The workload involves integrating 11 000 trajectories (each ~2.5 million steps) and training a shallow ANN on 10 000 samples for 3000 epochs; both tasks are CPU-bound and fit comfortably within a few GB of RAM, with no GPU requirement.
